query: How must weighted interfaces be normalized and what mandatory metadata fields (weight_unit, measurement_scale, aggregation_rule) are required in the schema?

response.query: How must weighted interfaces be normalized and what mandatory metadata fields (weight_unit, measurement_scale, aggregation_rule) are required in the schema?
response.answer: Weighted interfaces must be normalized by dividing by the sum of weights. Required metadata fields include weight_unit, measurement_scale, and aggregation_rule. These ensure proper interpretation and aggregation of weighted data.

results.title: University of Dundee A starting guide to root ecology Freschet ...
results.content: Consideration of the below-New Phytologist (2021) 232: 973–1122 www.newphytologist.com  2021 The Authors New Phytologist  2021 New Phytologist Foundation Forum Community resources New Phytologist 974 Key words: below-ground ecology, handbook, plant root functions, protocol, root classiﬁcation, root ecology, root traits, trait measurements. A ﬁfth challenge is to strengthen the general understanding of root trait ecological meaning, and emphasise current limitations and promises in the use of these traits as proxies for plant and ecosystem functioning (Lalibert´ e, 2016; Freschet et al., 2021). Coupling measurements from several ﬁelds of root ecology is often needed to adequately capture speciﬁc plant and ecosystem functions (e.g. McCormack et al., 2017; Freschet et al., 2018), sometimes across different below-ground plant entities (Freschet & Roumet, 2017). In this context, adequately characterising root functions requires a priori knowledge of when (e.g. along seasonal cycles, daily cycles), where (e.g. across soil layers) and what below-ground entities (e.g. root orders) to sample, and what type of trait (e.g. morphological, architectural) to measure (Freschet et al., 2021).
